title: The Broom of the System (Penguin Orange Classics)

vibeProfile.oneLine: A woman wonders if she is real, or just a character, in Wallace's debut.

summary: David Foster Wallace's precocious first novel follows Lenore Beadsman, a switchboard operator whose great-grandmother, a former student of Wittgenstein, has vanished, as she wonders whether she is a real person or merely a character in someone's story. Playful, verbose and philosophically restless, it announced Wallace's obsessions, language, self-consciousness, whether meaning is possible, in a comic, chaotic package. Uneven but dazzling, it is a fascinating first look at one of the most influential writers of his generation.
whyReadIt: Wallace's dazzling, chaotic debut, already obsessed with language and selfhood. A fascinating first look at a singular mind.

funFacts.text: Wallace wrote it as his undergraduate thesis at Amherst College.
